title: Terminal-section derived comparisons compatible with Ext cocycles
statement: Let $f:Z\to X$ be continuous with additive abelian-sheaf pushforward $F=f_*$ [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Write $K_X,K_Z$ for sheafified free abelian terminal representables, $G=\Gamma(X,-)$, and $C_X^n,C_Z^n$ for the Ext-defined cohomology presheaf functors evaluated at the terminal opens. Suppose $a:K_X\to F(K_Z)$ takes each sheafified representable generator to its inverse-image generator followed by $f^{-1}(X)=Z$. There are natural isomorphisms $x_n:R^nG\simeq C_X^n$ and $z_n:R^n(FG)\simeq C_Z^n$, simultaneously for all $n\ge0$, with this normalization: for every sheaf $M$ on $Z$, injective resolutions $I$ of $M$ and $J$ of $F(M)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], augmented comparison $\phi:J\to F(I)$, and cocycles $s:K_X\to J^p$, $t:K_Z\to I^p$ satisfying $aF(t)=s\phi^p$, one has $z_p(M)(\rho_I^{-1}H^p(G\phi)\rho_J(x_p(F(M))^{-1}(J.\mathrm{extMk}(s))))=I.\mathrm{extMk}(t)$. The $\rho$ are canonical right-derived resolution comparisons [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. This states no spectral-object construction or spectral edge identification.

proof.text: Construct the additive Hom/section identification using the sheafification adjunction, the free abelian adjunction and Yoneda. On a map out of the free terminal sheaf, it evaluates the image of its terminal generator. Use its naturality degreewise to identify the Hom complex of every injective resolution with its section complex.

Compute Ext by the Hom complex and ordinary derived sections by the section complex; compose these explicit identifications on the chosen resolution to construct x_n, with naturality from resolution-map naturality. Do not choose an arbitrary isomorphism from the nonempty comparison theorem: use the underlying Hom-complex construction, so its value on extMk is the represented homology class.

The equality of terminal sections of f_*M and M, including transport across f^{-1}(top)=top, is an additive natural isomorphism. The generator formula for a says that precomposing F(t) with a corresponds to the same terminal section as t. Derive this natural isomorphism and compose with the Z analogue of x to construct z_n.

For arbitrary I,J,phi, apply the degreewise Hom/section identification to s and t. The given relation aF(t)=s phi sends the cocycle represented by s to the cocycle represented by t. Homology of G(phi) thus has the required effect. Naturality of the canonical right-derived resolution computations and independence of injective-resolution comparisons give the equation for all supplied resolutions and comparisons.
